A_target.statement:
Let $f$ be [[Definition:Differentiable Real Function|differentiable]] at $x_0$.
Then the [[Definition:Tangent Line|tangent line]] to $y = \map f x$ at $x_0$ is:
:$y = \map f {x_0} + \map {f'} {x_0} \paren {x - x_0}$

B_source.statement:
Let $f$ be differentiable at $x_0$.
Then:
:$\map {f'} {x_0} = \displaystyle \lim_{h \mathop \to 0} \frac {\map f {x_0 + h} - \map f {x_0} } h$
the limit of slopes of [[Definition:Secant Line|secant lines]].

substitutions.a secant line through two nearby points: a discrete approximation to the tangent
substitutions.the second point x0 + h: a point approaching x0 as h -> 0

object_map.reformulation: Approximate the tangent by secant lines through pairs of points and pass to the limit as the points merge.

validity_conditions: f is differentiable at x0, so the secant slopes converge to a finite limit f'(x0).
Each secant is an exact line through two points; the tangent is their limit as h -> 0.
This is a discrete-to-continuous (finite-secant to limiting-tangent) approximation.
proof_plan: Form the [[Definition:Secant Line|secant]] through $\tuple {x_0, \map f {x_0} }$ and $\tuple {x_0 + h, \map f {x_0 + h} }$.

Its slope is:
:$\dfrac {\map f {x_0 + h} - \map f {x_0} } h$

Let $h \to 0$.
By differentiability, the slope tends to $\map {f'} {x_0}$.

The limiting line through $\tuple {x_0, \map f {x_0} }$ with slope $\map {f'} {x_0}$ is:
:$y = \map f {x_0} + \map {f'} {x_0} \paren {x - x_0}$
which is the tangent line.
{{qed}}
